title: Non-Egress Upgrade Flow: Validation, Canary, and Fallback Criteria for Sealed VPCs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a deterministic, testable acceptance contract for performing control-plane and operator upgrades in customer VPCs that cannot permit unrestricted egress. This doc covers a minimal-egress upgrade mode that: (1) allows short, auditable artifact fetches only during narrow maintenance windows; (2) validates upgrades deterministically with canary nodes and checksum attestations; and (3) defines automated fallback and operator rollback criteria for sealed or air-gapped environments. Goal is to provide a single, auditable upgrade path that preserves zero/limited-egress policies while minimizing customer operator burden.
requirements: Minimal-egress upgrade mode must support two authentication patterns: pre-seeded artifact mirror (customer-provided) and ephemeral signed fetch through a customer-approved jump-proxy
Upgrade artifacts must be cryptographically signed and include a reproducible checksum bundle; operator must verify signatures against customer-provided root before applying
Maintenance window negotiation: console/operator API must accept a proposed maintenance window and a signed consent token from the customer network admin
Canary topology: designate 2% of operator pods (min 2) as canary targets in each cluster; canaries must complete smoke checks before global rollout
Deterministic health checks: binary-level integrity, container image digest match, operator API schema compatibility, and control-plane reconcile latency thresholds
Rollback gates: automatic rollback if canary failure rate > 10% or control-plane reconciliation time degrades > 2x baseline for > 10 minutes
Telemetry and redaction: telemetry emitted during upgrade must be scrubbed of customer network identifiers; telemetry must include artifact digest, step timestamp, and outcome codes
Audit trail: every upgrade action (initiate, approve, fetch, verify, apply, promote, rollback) must be recorded with operator and customer approver identity and signed audit token
Operator offline validation: upgrade plan must be verifiable against a local artifact mirror (checksums & signature validation) without contacting Redwood control plane
Support matrix: documented operator compatibility matrix for kernel versions, CNI variants, and common enterprise proxies (eg. BlueGate, Bastionless), and minimum operator version for staged rollback
acceptance_criteria: Can initiate a minimal-egress upgrade from Console or API with a customer-supplied consent token and maintenance window; request persists if network connectivity is intermittent

Operator performs artifact signature and checksum validation using only local mirrors or ephemeral proxy within the maintenance window; validation failures are logged and surfaced to both customer and Redwood ops
Canary nodes complete a predefined smoke test suite (CRDs reconcile, runtime kv-cache warm, sample inference request latency baseline within 1.5x) before the rollout proceeds
If canary failures exceed thresholds, the system triggers an automated rollback to the previous operator image within the same maintenance window and notifies stakeholders

When operating in sealed mode (no egress allowed), the operator validates the upgrade plan from a pre-seeded artifact bundle and produces an attestable verification report that can be provided to the customer
All upgrade steps produce signed audit records (operator identity + customer approver) and store a hash of the audit in an append-only log accessible to the customer
Telemetry emitted during the upgrade contains no raw IPs, MACs, or other private network identifiers; audit preserves minimal identity tokens only
End-to-end test harness reproduces upgrade in a simulated sealed VPC (CI job) and completes within the agreed timebox for the maintenance window (configurable; default 60 minutes)
test_plan: CI: Create a sealed VPC test fixture with pre-seeded artifact mirror, run upgrade flow using ephemeral consent token, assert audit and telemetry policies
Canary failure simulation: Inject a controlled reconciliation error in canary pods and assert automatic rollback within 5 minutes of detection
Egress-limited mode: Verify operator can proceed using a customer-approved jump-proxy that only permits TLS+mutual-auth to artifact mirror endpoints
Offline validation: Run a plan validation tool that consumes a downloaded artifact bundle and reproduces signature and checksum verification without any external network calls
Fuzz test maintenance negotiation: Randomize maintenance window start/end times and ensure system queues and resumes upgrade attempts across intermittent connectivity
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal dry run: infra team validates the flow on staging sealed clusters (no customer data) and signs off on telemetry redaction
Phase 1 - Pilot: 2 customer opt-in pilots in different network topologies (one proxyless, one with controlled jump-proxy); support engineer on-call
Phase 2 - Gradual ramp: Expand to customers with similar operator versions using 24h rolling windows and automated canary gating
Phase 3 - General availability: Enable default minimal-egress upgrade option in Console with explicit customer consent flow and required audit retention policy
rollback_plan: Automated rollback hook: If canary gates fail, the controller reverts the operator image and configuration to the last known good digest and re-runs smoke checks
Manual rollback: Support runbook with CLI and Console steps to force immediate revert; require two approvers (support engineer + customer admin) for emergency revert outside maintenance window
Post-rollback verification: After rollback, a verification pass must run to validate cluster state and produce an incident artifact linking to telemetry and audit logs
Incident retrospective: Any rollback triggers a required postmortem and a retro ticket in ENG indicating root cause and mitigation plan
telemetry_and_alerting: Metric: upgrade_step_duration_seconds labeled by step and outcome
Alert: canary_failure_rate > 10% sustained for 10 minutes (pager to on-call)
Audit export: daily signed digest of upgrade audit events available to customer S3 mirror or equivalent
Log redaction: PII and network surface fields must be removed prior to leaving customer VPC when telemetry is forwarded
open_questions: Consent token format: prefer short-lived signed JWT vs customer-supplied opaque token — which is easier for SSO/SAML customers to adopt?
Mirror verification: should we publish a small validation container (OCI) customers can run to pre-validate mirrors, or rely on operator-only verification?
Maintenance window length: default 60 minutes — is that sufficient for largest operator upgrades (answer expected from ENG-71234)
Customer audit retention: how long should Redwood retain signed audit digests for customers who opt into shared telemetry?
notes: This PRD intentionally separates artifact fetch from validation so customers with strict egress policies can provide mirrors ahead of time.
We aim to minimize human-in-the-loop steps: only approval for maintenance window needed unless rollback requires emergency approval
Coordinate with Security for signature verification libraries and potential integration with customer KMS for root-of-trust verification
Work with Console team to prototype the consent token UX and the maintenance window scheduler
